what_it_does: Hydrates skin and softens rough, thickened patches by binding water and loosening dead skin buildup.
summary_short: Urea is a proven moisturizing ingredient that helps the skin hold water and feel smoother. At low levels it mainly hydrates; at higher levels it can soften rough, scaly, or callused skin. It may sting on cracked or irritated skin.
summary_long:
Urea is part of the skin’s natural moisturizing factor, a group of water-binding substances that help keep the outer layer of skin flexible and hydrated. In skincare, it acts as a humectant, drawing water into the stratum corneum and helping reduce dryness, tightness, and flaking.

Its effect depends strongly on concentration. Around 2–10%, urea is mostly used as a moisturizer and barrier-supportive hydrator. Around 10–20%, it can also help soften rough texture and loosen compacted dead skin. Higher strengths, often used for very thick calluses, cracked heels, or nail issues, are more treatment-like and may be too intense for routine facial use.

Urea has better practical support than many trendy moisturizing ingredients, especially for dry, rough, scaly, or compromised skin. It is commonly used in body creams for conditions such as xerosis, keratosis pilaris, rough elbows, and cracked feet, though severe or persistent skin conditions should be managed with a clinician.

The main drawback is irritation potential. Urea can sting or burn when applied to open cracks, freshly exfoliated skin, eczema flares, or a damaged barrier, especially at higher concentrations. Sensitive facial skin should usually start with low-strength products and avoid combining it with too many other exfoliating ingredients at once.

Urea pairs well with glycerin, ceramides, petrolatum, dimethicone, lactic acid, and other barrier-supportive ingredients. It can be used alongside exfoliating acids or retinoids in some routines, but layering several strong active products may increase dryness or stinging.
quick_facts: Part of skin’s natural moisturizing factor
Low levels hydrate; higher levels soften rough skin
Useful for dry, flaky, or callused areas
Can sting on cracked or irritated skin
Common in body, hand, and foot creams
